sections.name: AnimatedCounterProps
sections.title: Animated number display
sections.what: Counts a number up from zero to the target over about 0.8 seconds by default, showing the chosen decimal places and suffix. The count is driven by the screen's redraw steps.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives stats a polished count-up effect. Reason for the default timing not stated.
sections.watch_out: The animation loop is not stopped when the component is removed or the target changes, so it can keep running in the background.

summary: A number display that counts up smoothly from zero to a target value.
purpose: Makes statistics feel lively when the analytics screen loads.
why: Likely reason: a visual effect that makes numbers more engaging. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Starts a counter at zero. On each animation frame, works out how far through the set duration the animation is and shows that share of the target, with the chosen decimal places and suffix. Stops when it reaches the target. Restarts whenever the target or duration changes.
inputs: value: the target number. duration: time in milliseconds, default 800. suffix: text after the number, such as hours. decimals: digits after the decimal point, default 0.
outputs: An animated number on screen. No data is saved.
risks: The animation loop is never cancelled, so if the number leaves the screen mid-animation it may still try to update. Quick changes can start several loops at once. Each change restarts the count from zero.
debug: If the number jumps or flickers, check that value is a real number and not text. If warnings appear after leaving a screen, the animation loop is probably still running. If the timing feels wrong, check the duration.
